concepts.en: Place value and rounding decimal numbers

summary.big_en: Every digit has a value that depends on its place. Rounding replaces a number with a nearby simpler one.

topics.title: Place value
topics.subtitle: value | position
topics.def: The place value of a digit is the value it has because of its position in the number.
rules: Understand the value of each digit in a decimal number.
Moving a digit one place to the left makes it ten times bigger.

topics.title: Compose, decompose, regroup
topics.def: Composing builds a number from its parts, decomposing breaks it back down, and regrouping writes the same total a different way.
rules: Write a number in expanded form (compose).
Break a number into its place values (decompose).
Group the values a different way, keeping the same total (regroup).

topics.title: Word form
topics.subtitle: read & write
topics.def: Word form is a number written out in words instead of digits.
rules: Write and read decimal numbers in words.
After the decimal point, say the digits one by one.

topics.title: Multiply & divide by 10, 100, 1000
topics.def: Multiplying or dividing by 10, 100 or 1000 slides every digit along the place value columns.
rules: Multiply or divide a decimal number by 10, 100 or 1000.
Every digit moves 1, 2 or 3 places: left to multiply, right to divide.

topics.title: Rounding
topics.subtitle: rounding off
topics.def: Rounding replaces a number with the nearest simpler number in the place you choose.
rules: Round a number with 2 decimal places to the nearest tenth or whole number.
Look at the digit just after the place you are rounding to.

branches.then: keep the tenths digit the same

branches.when: Nearest whole number · tenths digit is 5, 6, 7, 8, 9
Nearest whole number · tenths digit is 0, 1, 2, 3, 4
branches.then: keep the ones digit the same

glossary.def: One of the symbols 0 to 9 that a number is written with.
glossary.example: The digit 7 in 213.807 stands for 7 thousandths (p.13).

glossary.def: The value a digit has because of its position in the number.
glossary.example: In 6703.46 the 7 has a place value of 7 hundreds (p.13).

glossary.def: The dot that separates the whole-number part from the part smaller than one.
The first place after the decimal point.
glossary.example: In 13.136 the 1 after the point is 1 tenth (p.13).

glossary.def: The second place after the decimal point.
The third place after the decimal point.
Putting parts together to make a number.
Splitting a number into the parts it is made of.
Writing the same number as a different set of parts.
glossary.example: 56.079 is also 56 ones and 79 thousandths (WB p.9).

glossary.def: Replace a number with a nearby number that is easier to use.
The closest of the possible answers.
A number written with a decimal point, so it can show parts smaller than one.

summary.big_en: A sequence follows a rule. Knowing the rule lets you find any term without writing them all out.

topics.title: Counting on and counting back
topics.def: Counting on and back means adding or subtracting the same amount each time to make a sequence.
rules: Count forward and backward in steps of constant size.
The step can be a fraction or a decimal, not just a whole number.

topics.title: Position to term rule
topics.def: A position-to-term rule turns a term's position number straight into the term itself.
rules: A term-to-term rule tells you the next term; a position-to-term rule tells you any term.
Use the position-to-term rule to jump straight to a far-off term.

topics.title: Square numbers
topics.def: A square number is what you get when you multiply a number by itself.
rules: Work out the square number in any position: the ninth square number is 9 × 9 = 81.
Use the small 2 notation to mean squared.

topics.title: Cube numbers
topics.def: A cube number is what you get when you multiply a number by itself three times.
rules: Know the cube of numbers up to 5.
Cubing means multiplying a number by itself three times.

topics.title: Common multiples and common factors
topics.def: A common multiple is shared by the times tables of two numbers; a common factor divides exactly into both.
rules: A common multiple is in the times table of both numbers.
A common factor divides into both numbers exactly.

glossary.def: One of the numbers in a sequence.
Where a term sits in the sequence: first, second, third and so on.
A rule that takes you from one term to the next.
A rule that gives the term from its position.
glossary.example: Multiply the position by 2, so the 50th term is 100 (p.23).

glossary.def: The result of multiplying a number by itself.
The result of multiplying a number by itself three times.
A number in another number's times table.
A number that divides into another number exactly.
A multiple that two or more numbers share.
glossary.example: 24 is a common multiple of 3 and 8 (p.30).

glossary.def: A factor that two or more numbers share.
glossary.example: The common factors of 18 and 24 are 1, 2, 3 and 6 (p.32).

flashcards.front_en: Name the three places after the decimal point.
flashcards.back_en: Tenths, hundredths, thousandths.

flashcards.front_en: What happens to the digits when you multiply by 1000?
flashcards.back_en: Every digit moves three places to the left.

flashcards.front_en: What happens to the digits when you divide by 100?
flashcards.back_en: Every digit moves two places to the right.

flashcards.front_en: Rounding to the nearest tenth: which digit do you look at?
flashcards.back_en: The hundredths digit. 0–4 rounds down, 5–9 rounds up.

flashcards.front_en: Rounding to the nearest whole number: which digit do you look at?
flashcards.back_en: The tenths digit, using the same 0–4 down, 5–9 up rule.

flashcards.front_en: How many decimal places has an answer rounded to the nearest tenth?
flashcards.back_en: Always one, even if it is zero.

flashcards.front_en: What does it mean to regroup a number?
flashcards.back_en: Write the same number as a different set of parts, with the same total.

flashcards.front_en: How do you read the digits after a decimal point?
flashcards.back_en: One by one: 2.139 is two point one three nine.

flashcards.front_en: What does a position-to-term rule do?
flashcards.back_en: Gives any term straight from its position, without listing them all.

flashcards.front_en: What is the ninth square number?
flashcards.back_en: 81, because 9 × 9 = 81.

quiz.stem_en: What is the value of the digit 7 in 6703.46?
quiz.why_en: The 7 sits in the hundreds column (p.13).

quiz.stem_en: What is the value of the digit 7 in 213.807?
quiz.why_en: It is the third place after the decimal point (p.13).

quiz.stem_en: What is the value of the digit 7 in 456.702?
quiz.why_en: It is the first place after the decimal point (p.13).

quiz.stem_en: What does the digit 5 in 3.065 represent?
quiz.why_en: It is the third place after the decimal point (WB p.9).

quiz.stem_en: How many times bigger is the value of the digit 6 in 64.53 than the value of the digit 6 in 0.367?
quiz.why_en: 6 tens against 6 hundredths is three places, so 1000 times (p.19).

quiz.stem_en: In the number 13.136, which digit is in the hundredths place?
quiz.why_en: Hundredths is the second place after the decimal point (p.13).

quiz.stem_en: What is 5.6 × 100?
quiz.why_en: Every digit moves two places to the left (WB p.11).
Every digit moves three places to the left (WB p.11).

quiz.stem_en: What is 670 ÷ 1000?
quiz.why_en: Every digit moves three places to the right (WB p.11).

quiz.stem_en: What is 191 ÷ 100?
quiz.why_en: Every digit moves two places to the right (WB p.11).

quiz.stem_en: Find the missing number: ___ × 0.9 = 9
quiz.why_en: 0.9 must move one place to the left, so multiply by 10 (p.19).

quiz.stem_en: Find the missing number: 705 ÷ ___ = 7.05
quiz.why_en: The digits move two places to the right, so divide by 100 (p.19).

quiz.stem_en: A number is multiplied by 10, then by 10 again, then by 10 again, and the answer is 7. What was the starting number?
quiz.why_en: Three multiplications by 10 is × 1000, so reverse it: 7 ÷ 1000 (WB p.12).

quiz.stem_en: Write 10 + 3 + 1 tenth + 3 hundredths + 6 thousandths as a decimal number.
quiz.why_en: Each part goes in its own place value column (p.13).

quiz.stem_en: Copy and complete: 87.655 = 80 + 7 + ___
quiz.why_en: The decimal part decomposes into 6 tenths, 5 hundredths and 5 thousandths (p.19).

quiz.stem_en: What decimal number is 90 + 7 + 3 tenths + 1 hundredth + 4 thousandths?
quiz.why_en: Put each part in its place value column (p.19).

quiz.stem_en: Magda regroups 56.079. Which of these is NOT the same number?
quiz.why_en: 56 + 0.79 is 56.79, which is ten times bigger in the decimal part (WB p.9).

quiz.stem_en: Which expression is equal to 4.063?
quiz.why_en: 6 is in the hundredths place and 3 in the thousandths place (WB p.11).

quiz.stem_en: Why do we round numbers?

choices.en: To make them easier to describe and understand

quiz.why_en: Rounding makes numbers easier to describe and understand (p.16).

quiz.stem_en: What is 4.09 rounded to the nearest whole number?
quiz.why_en: The tenths digit is 0, so round down (p.16).

quiz.stem_en: What is 7.45 rounded to the nearest whole number?
quiz.why_en: The tenths digit is 4, which is in 0–4, so round down (p.16).

quiz.stem_en: A book costs $14.65. What is that to the nearest dollar?
quiz.why_en: The tenths digit is 6, so round up (p.16).

quiz.stem_en: What is 9.55 rounded to the nearest whole number?
quiz.why_en: The tenths digit is 5, so round up from 9 to 10 (p.19).

quiz.stem_en: What is 8.80 rounded to the nearest tenth?
quiz.why_en: The hundredths digit is 0, so round down (p.16).

quiz.stem_en: What is 3.95 rounded to the nearest tenth?
quiz.why_en: The hundredths digit 5 rounds the tenths digit up from 9, carrying into the ones (p.16).

quiz.stem_en: What is 3.08 rounded to the nearest tenth?
quiz.why_en: The hundredths digit is 8, so round up (p.19).

quiz.stem_en: What is 9.07 rounded to the nearest tenth?
quiz.why_en: The hundredths digit is 7, so round up (p.17).

quiz.stem_en: Which of these rounds to 7.5 to the nearest tenth?
quiz.why_en: 7.49 has hundredths digit 9, so the 4 tenths round up to 5 (p.17).

quiz.stem_en: Rounded to the nearest tenth, how many decimal places must the answer always have?

choices.en: Exactly one, even if it is zero
As many as the original number

quiz.why_en: There must always be one decimal place in the answer (p.16).

quiz.stem_en: Is this true: 3.04 is 3 to the nearest whole number and 3 to the nearest tenth?

choices.en: No — to the nearest tenth it is 3.0
No, to the nearest whole number it is 4

quiz.why_en: A number rounded to the nearest tenth keeps one decimal place (p.17).

quiz.stem_en: How do you write 2.139 in words?

choices.en: Two point one hundred and thirty-nine

quiz.why_en: After the decimal point the digits are said one by one (p.14).

quiz.stem_en: Which number is 'twenty point four three one'?
quiz.why_en: Twenty, then the digits 4, 3, 1 after the point (p.14).

quiz.stem_en: How do you write 0.375 in words?
quiz.why_en: The digits after the point are read separately (p.12, p.14).

quiz.stem_en: A sequence starts at 2 and the rule is add 3. What are the next three terms?
quiz.why_en: Add 3 each time: 2, 5, 8, 11 (p.22).

quiz.stem_en: The first term is 4 and the term-to-term rule is add 7. What is the fourth term?
A sequence counts back in steps of 0.2 from 1. What comes after 0.6?
quiz.why_en: Each step subtracts 0.2 (p.22).

quiz.stem_en: A sequence has terms 2, 4, 6, 8. What is the position-to-term rule?
quiz.why_en: Position 1 gives 2, position 2 gives 4, so multiply by 2 (p.23).

quiz.stem_en: With the position-to-term rule 'multiply by 2', what is the 50th term?
With the position-to-term rule 'multiply by 4', what is the 25th term?
What is the difference between a term-to-term rule and a position-to-term rule?

choices.en: They are two names for the same thing
Term-to-term only works for even numbers
Position-to-term only works for the first ten terms
Term-to-term gives the next term; position-to-term gives any term straight away

quiz.why_en: The position-to-term rule lets you find any term without writing them all out (p.22).

quiz.stem_en: What is the ninth square number?
What is 7²?
What does the small 2 in 5² mean?
quiz.why_en: The notation 2 means squared (p.27).

quiz.stem_en: Which two square numbers add up to 45?
What is 5³?
What is 3³?
Which is larger, 2³ or 3²?
Which two cube numbers add up to 152?
Which number is a multiple of both 3 and 5 and less than 20?
quiz.why_en: 15 is in both the 3 and 5 times tables (p.30).

quiz.stem_en: What are the factors of 18?
quiz.why_en: These are the numbers that divide 18 exactly (p.32).

quiz.stem_en: What are the common factors of 18 and 24?
quiz.why_en: They are the factors that appear in both lists (p.32).

quiz.stem_en: Which numbers are factors of both 30 and 20?
quiz.why_en: These divide both 30 and 20 exactly (p.32).

quiz.stem_en: All the common multiples of 3 and 8 that are less than 50 are:
quiz.why_en: 24 and 48 are in both times tables and below 50 (p.32).

quiz.stem_en: Two sequences go 3, 6, 9, 12 … and 5, 10, 15, 20 … Which number over 100 is in both?
quiz.why_en: 105 is a multiple of both 3 and 5 (p.32).
